$comment: Riftlight opening, chapter 2 (docs/campaigns/continental-rift/arc.md, glacier-survival). Revised in November 2026: question "Can we get the kid home and find somewhere warm?". The yetis take the party in, the kid gets home, the party learns the snow on the quay came from here, the melt has been strange since the mountain woke (true after every Gemfall ending), and loose snow drifts back uphill (the first "moved things go home" image). Keeps the Conservatory and the low song (learned_glacier_note, tested_singing_seam, one of marked_glacier_drift / sheltered_kid_on_detour / found_drift_hollow).
title: A Bell in the Snow

plate.narration: A little snowhorn goat bleats across the meltwater. Its herd answers from a snowy ledge, bells clinking. Between them, the water runs cold and quick. Those small hooves need a way home.

goal.text: Can we get the kid home and find somewhere warm?

steps.label: Get the goat back to its herd
Get everyone in from the cold

arrival.narration: The bell rings again, and the kid answers with an enormous bleat. You brush snow off its knees, scraped in the scramble on the quay. So this is where the snow on the quay came from: a whole white mountainside. Across the slope, a herd of snowhorn goats waits on a ledge. Between you, a melt channel cuts through the snow. Far off, a deep voice calls, "Hoo-up! Hoo-up!" Can you get the little goat home to its herd, and find somewhere warm for everyone?

shelter.narration: Wind presses your wet clothes to your knees. The kid is shivering. A bank of packed snow would block the wind. Or you could follow a row of dark rocks nearer the bell. What do you do first? "Meh," says the kid, which clearly means hurry up.

windbreak.narration: You scrape a hollow behind the bank and huddle close. The kid noses under the warmest arm. From here you can see footprints between the dark rocks, each wider than your head. "Hoo-up!" calls the far voice. The kid's ears swivel toward it.

rocks.narration: The rocks give your feet something firm under the snow. Beside them are deep footprints. A broad wooden sled has scraped a track toward the bell. "Hoo-up!" calls the far voice, somewhere ahead.

mend.narration: Gentle light settles over the kid's scraped knees. It stops shaking long enough to chew your sleeve. Between the rocks, you spot broad footprints. "Meh-heh," says the kid, which sounds a lot like thank you.

wind_warm.narration: The wind finds every wet seam, and your sleeves crackle with ice. You stamp and rub until the ice cracks off in crumbs. Damp now, not frozen. The kid sneezes a tiny cloud. "Hoo-up!" calls the far voice again, closer.

kid_burrow.narration: Warm enough to be bold, the kid wriggles out of your coat and dives under one of three snow mounds, all the same shape. Then the mounds start to move.

interaction.cue: Watch the mound the kid hides under, then pick where it is.

onSuccess.narration: There it is, wearing a snow hat! Back into your coat it goes.

onFailure.narration: Empty! And empty again! A snowy nose pokes out of the third mound and sneezes, very pleased with itself. Back into your coat it goes.

onAssisted.narration: You listen hard. A tiny bleat gives it away.

prints.narration: Past the rocks, the snow is stamped with footprints wide as dinner plates. The wind is filling them in. Some lead toward the bell. Some wander off, as if the walker forgot where they were going. Which line do you trust? "Hoo-up! Hoo-up!" The voice is closer now, and very deep.

prints_read.prompt: Whoever has the sharpest eyes, find the freshest line of prints.
prints_read.narration: Fresh prints have sharp edges. Old ones are soft as pillows. "Hoo-up!" calls the far voice.

onSuccess.narration: Sharp edges, fresh snow. The line bends toward the bell.

onFailure.narration: Your line ends at a bare patch where the walker sat down to think. You backtrack, grumbling, and find the right one.

prints_march.prompt: March along the prints before the wind fills them in!
prints_march.narration: The prints are far apart. It is like hopping across a giant's stepping stones. "Hoo-up!" calls the far voice.

onSuccess.narration: Print by print, you hop along toward the bell.

onFailure.narration: A foot misses and sinks to the knee. By the time you dig it out, the line has almost vanished. You catch it just in time.

prints_air.prompt: Use skyward or glide to look down at the whole trail.
prints_air.narration: Wings lift you above the wind, where the whole trail shows at once. Far below, someone calls, "Hoo-up!"

onSuccess.narration: From up high the line is plain, and you point everyone along it.

onFailure.narration: The wind tosses the view into a swirl. You come down and follow your nose instead. It mostly works.

tracks.narration: A yeti herder comes around the ridge, pulling an empty sled. "Hoo-up!" she calls, and then she stops at the sight of the kid. "There you are, you little snowball." The kid is from her herd. Then she sees the rest of you. "Did you come with the weather?"

variants.text: She looks back at your line of stones. "You marked the hollow. That helps the next person through."
She checks the kid with one broad hand. "Still warm. That long way around was well chosen."
You point out the hollow behind you. She nods. "You found your own way out. Keep that rope."

tell_rift.narration: You tell her about the snow on the quay and the tear in the air. The yeti looks at your wet boots and harbor rope. "Snow on a harbor, from a clear sky?" She looks up at the high field, which is bare as a plate. "So that is where my snow went." She digs a honeycake out of her apron. "For the news. Now, walk on the dark ice when I say. Never the white." She lays a folded blanket on the sled.

ask_help.narration: "First, we get you warm," says the yeti. She wraps a folded blanket around the kid and your arms together, and it is warm as toast. She sniffs your coats. "Harbor slush? Then that is where my snow went. The glacier keeps surprising me." She turns the sled toward the melt channel.

herder_gift.narration: At the channel, the herder looks you over. "You kept that kid warm all the way here. Good." She hands you a bundle wrapped in a cloth. "Bread, cheese, and a sausage that has not made up its mind." She points across the water. "The herd is over there. First, we read the ice."

read_water.prompt: Whoever reads ice best, pick the edges that will hold.
read_water.narration: The ice comes in two kinds. Dark ice holds a boot. Sugary white ice holds nothing. "Tell me what you see," says the herder.

onSuccess.narration: You trace a line of dark ice. The herder nods at every patch.

onFailure.narration: You pick a sugar patch. The herder's boot crunches through. "That taught us both." You look again and find the dark line.

channel.narration: Meltwater gurgles through a narrow gap. The snow bridge sags when the herder tests it. A flat stone sticks out upstream. The herder points out dark patches of ice. "Those will hold a careful foot." The herd waits on the far side.

step.prompt: Step across the stone without slipping into the meltwater.

onSuccess.narration: You land on the far bank and pass the kid across.

onFailure.narration: Your foot slips into icy water. The herder catches your wrist and lifts you onto the bank.

step.narration: "One foot on the stone, one foot on me," says the herder, holding out a huge hand.

sledge.prompt: Hold the sled steady while everyone crosses.

onSuccess.narration: You brace the runners against the stone. The party crawls over one at a time.

onFailure.narration: A runner slips. The herder grabs the sled and you scramble across, soaked to the elbows.

sledge.narration: "Hold her steady," says the herder, patting the sled. "She is old, and she wobbles."

wing_line.prompt: Wings carry the rope to the far bank. Can you guide the line around the sharp ice?

onSuccess.narration: You guide the line clear of the sharp ice and tie it to a rock on the far bank. It steadies everyone crossing.

onFailure.narration: The line snags on sharp ice. You free it, splashing one foot into the channel.

wing_line.narration: "Show-off," says the herder, grinning. "Go on, then."

song_step.prompt: A Songkeeper sets a steady pace. Can you lead everyone along the dark patches in time?

onSuccess.narration: You call the steps in time with the song. Everyone follows the herder's safe footholds.

onFailure.narration: Your foot slips between two beats. The herder pulls you clear and leads the last steps herself.

song_step.narration: "Sing it slow," says the herder. "Goats like slow."

dry_bank.narration: The kid sees the herd and wriggles free. A shaggy goat sniffs it nose to tail, then tucks it between her front legs. The herder checks on everyone. "All back. Good."

wet_bank.narration: The herder wrings out your sleeve over the channel. "We will dry that indoors." The kid has already run to a shaggy goat, who sniffs it all over and will not let it move.

settle.narration: The herd crowds around the kid, bells clanking like a kitchen drawer. A shaggy lead goat with one chipped horn sniffs everyone in turn. "They won't go indoors while they are upset," says the herder. "Settle them first."

settle_count.narration: Every goat wears a different bell: a clank, a tink, a cowbell, a spoon on a pot. Counting moving goats is like counting raindrops, but every bell is here. The goats calm down. Someone finally knows who they are. "Twenty-two," says the herder, pleased. "And one small snowball makes twenty-three."

settle_brush.narration: The goats' wool has frozen into ice beads that rattle as they walk. They hold still for brushing, if you find the itchy spot. Soon the herd sounds like a rattle full of calm. "Behind the ears," says the herder. "That is where they keep their worries."

settle_feed.narration: You unwrap the supper. The lead goat sniffs the cheese and sneezes. Then she eats the crust, gives you a forgiving look, and leads the herd to the herder. "Spoiled," says the herder fondly.

settle_lull.narration: You hum a slow tune that sounds like a blanket. The lead goat's ears droop. The spoon bell goes quiet. One by one, the goats stop stamping and follow the tune. "Now you are showing off," says the herder, smiling.

herd.narration: "In you go," calls the herder, waving the goats toward a low opening in the ice. The kid plants its feet. From inside comes a deep note that trembles through your boots, and the kid tilts its head to listen. Do you pick it up and carry it in? Or hum along with the note it is listening to?

choices.label: Pick it up and carry it

carry.narration: You scoop the kid up. It kicks like a drum solo, and every hoof finds a shin. "That works," says the herder, rubbing her own shin. "Once." In you all go, bruised but quick.

hum_door.prompt: Hum low and steady with the note from inside, so the kid follows the sound.
hum_door.narration: "Gently," whispers the herder. "It is listening for its own."

onSuccess.narration: You hum low, under the deep note. The kid tilts its head. From inside the ice, another voice hums back, right at you. The kid follows the sound, and you follow the kid. "Huh," says the herder. "The hall answered you."

onFailure.narration: Your hum comes out as a squeak. The kid sits down in the snow, offended, and so do you. It takes a long, cold time. At last it butts your elbow and trots inside. "Patience is cold work," says the herder. "But it works."

hall.narration: Inside is a singing hall carved from ice. Yetis sit on benches with warm cups, humming one low note together. The herder hangs your wet things by a row of warm stones. Damp blankets hang over a rail. "Glacier of Origins," she says. "You may stop arriving now." At the back, warm air drifts from a glass door.

variants.text: A young yeti singer points at you. "You hummed at the door! I heard you. You are halfway to the low song already."

hall_table.narration: At the long table, a round yeti knitter is making a scarf so long it runs under the bench and out the other side. She holds up goat-wool boot laces. "Three coins a pair. Quickest laces on the glacier. Or sit and be warm for free."

hall_dry.narration: You set your boots on the warm stones. Steam rises, and a small pond runs out of each one. The knitter hangs your socks on her scarf, which is what the scarf is for. "Socks on the scarf, boots on the stones," says the knitter. "That is the rule."

variants.text: Your boots steam on the warm stones. The dry crossing paid off: they are only damp. The knitter hangs your socks on her scarf, which is what the scarf is for.

hall_buy.narration: You count three coins into the knitter's mitten. She ties the laces into your boots with a speedy bow. "Go on, run. Do not trip. They are fast laces."

hall_share.narration: You break the supper in two and give the knitter the bigger half. She eats the sausage first, politely. Then she hands you a small whistle carved from goat horn. "For calling a herd off thin snow. One loud note. Do not blow it indoors."

conservatory.narration: Behind the glass door is a warm greenhouse full of song. This school is called the Conservatory. Here students learn to be a Songkeeper, a hero who heals with songs. A yeti named Aunt Bellow conducts with a carrot, and every plant leans toward whoever sings best. Above the door hangs a song bell on a cord. It holds a Songkeeper's songs, and it will not ring near a thorn bracer. "Anyone may try it on," says Aunt Bellow.

variants.text: Aunt Bellow waves her carrot. "Back to the Conservatory? Good." Every plant turns to see who came in. The song bell waits above the door for anyone who wants it.

conservatory_sing.narration: Aunt Bellow points her carrot at you. You sing. A sunflower turns to look. Then a fern. Then, very slowly, a shy little cactus. "The cactus never turns," Aunt Bellow whispers. "Keep singing."

listen.narration: A young yeti stops singing to turn a page in an open songbook. The note thins, then another singer fills it. "What is it for?" you ask. "For listening," says the herder. "A crack makes one sound. Running water makes another. The song helps us hear the difference." She pats the bench. "Low and steady. Try it. Nobody here learned by already knowing."

note_try.narration: The low note is lower than your voice wants to go. "Stand here," says the young yeti singer. "Hum from your boots."

interaction.cue: Listen to the young singer, then hum the pattern back.

onSuccess.narration: Your voices lock together like the teeth of a comb. The whole bench rumbles.

onFailure.narration: Your note slides like a goat on ice. Across the hall, the wall answers with a sharp crack, and frost showers the benches. Every yeti stops singing and looks at you. The second try, very quietly, wobbles into place.

onAssisted.narration: The young singer hums it slowly beside you until your voices settle.

learn_note.narration: You find the note together. It shakes at first, then settles. Across the hall, frost trembles off a sealed seam in the wall. The herder lays a palm on it. "That seam was quiet yesterday."

variants.text: The herder brushes frost out of her fur. "Low and steady. Not loud and wobbly. The ice listens to both."

changing.narration: "The melt has been strange since the mountain woke," says the herder. "A path we used last week is water now. It led to the herd's sheltered grazing ledge. Now we eat stored hay, and the pile shrinks every day." She frowns at the window. "And some nights the snow blows uphill. Snow does not do that." Outside, a bell rings twice. Three travelers in dark cloaks are packing up camp beside the hall.

variants.text: "Your windbreak is useful too," she adds. "I can tell travelers where to shelter."
"And thank you for keeping everyone steady at the channel."

blankets.narration: You spread the last blanket over the rail. "Bring yourselves back if you pass this way," says the herder. The kid bumps your knee, then trots back to the herd.

ledge_look.narration: The herder leads you past the hall to a stream. Last week a path ran here. Now meltwater nibbles the snow shelf along the bank. "The herd won't walk where it can't see poles," she says. "And the hay must reach the lower pen by dark. Two jobs, one sled."

ledge_poles.prompt: Everyone grab a pole and plant a line along the safe edge.
ledge_poles.narration: Each pole must go in straight, or the goats will follow it into the stream. "Straight as a yeti's whiskers," says the herder.

onSuccess.narration: A row of poles marches down the bank, crooked as skinny dancers.

onFailure.narration: One pole leans like a tired flag. With frozen fingers, you straighten it.

ledge_hay.prompt: The strongest hero takes the front of the sled. Everyone else pushes.
ledge_hay.narration: The hay sled is heavy as a sleeping bear and slides like a happy one. "Push from the back," says the herder, "and do not ride it."

onSuccess.narration: The sled hisses down to the lower pen with a whole load of hay.

onFailure.narration: The sled gets away and slides down alone, scattering hay. The goats help pick it up, which means they eat some.

ledge_brace.prompt: Brace the snow shelf steady while the poles go in.
ledge_brace.narration: A thornguard plants both feet. The snow shelf creaks. The thornguard does not. "Hold, hold," says the herder.

onSuccess.narration: The shelf stops creaking, and the poles go in, one by one, in a straight row.

onFailure.narration: The shelf shifts, but the poles still go in. Everyone works fast and nobody breathes.

ledge_whistle.narration: You blow one loud note. Every goat lifts its head and trots off the thin snow in a line. "Well," says the herder. "That is a better whistle than mine." She plants the poles herself.

shelf_cross.narration: One last pole goes across the snow shelf. "The stream pauses between gulps," says the herder. "Step across when it goes quiet." The stream gulps. Then it goes quiet.

interaction.cue: Step when the marker reaches the quiet gap between the stream's gulps.

onSuccess.narration: You step across in the quiet, plant the pole, and hop back before the next gulp.

onFailure.narration: The stream gulps early and knocks your shins against the shelf. You scramble back, sore and dripping. The herder plants the last pole herself.

onAssisted.narration: The herder counts the gulps aloud. You cross on the count, and the pole goes in.

ledge_done.narration: The herder looks over the herd, the hay and the line of safe ground. "The glacier is changing," she says. "But it will not catch us today. Thank you." She looks at you a long moment. "You brought my kid home through the weather. You are welcome in the hall, always." Past the hall, the travelers wave from their camp.

kid_friend.narration: As you turn to go, something bumps the back of your knees. It is not the little goat you brought home. That one is asleep in a heap of goats. This kid goat is even smaller, white with brown spots, and so wiggly that her whole back end wags. "That spotted one has taken a shine to you," says the herder. "She is mine to give, and I give her gladly. The herd will be quieter." Do you ask the spotted kid goat along?

choices.label: Ask the spotted kid goat to come along
Say goodbye to the spotted kid goat

kid_along.narration: The spotted kid goat springs straight up like popcorn, then trots at your heels. "Mind your bootlaces," says the herder. "She eats them." Too late. One lace is already half gone.

kid_goodbye.narration: You scratch the spotted kid goat behind the ears. She wiggles one last wiggle, sneezes on your boot, and bounces back to the herd. "She will tell them all about you," says the herder.

departure.narration: Warm and dry, you step outside. The little goat you brought home stays with its herd, already asleep in a heap of goats. You know now where the snow on the quay came from: right here. But why is a glacier spilling onto a harbor, and why does its snow walk uphill? A griffin in a travel cloak is trying to fold a map while a unicorn stands on one corner. "It will not fold," he mutters. Neither has noticed that the corner is under her hoof.

variants.text: The herder waves from the blanket rail. "Dry blankets for the next arrivals. That matters."

drift.narration: A gust wipes the footprints smooth. Then something odd happens. The wind blows down the slope, but the loose snow drifts up it, back toward the ridge, like it is walking home. Even the harbor slush on your boots slides off and creeps uphill after it. The kid watches it go and bleats. Ahead, a white drift fills the gap between two dark ridges. The bell rings beyond it. How deep is the snow?

drift_probe.narration: You tie the rope to a rock and inch forward. Under a thin crust, the drift is hollow! You back out and leave small stones marking the safe way along its edge. "Meh!" says the kid from your arms, impressed.

drift_detour.narration: You take turns sheltering the kid in your coats and follow the rocks around the drift. The walk is longer, but nobody falls in. "Meh," the kid grumbles, warm and sleepy in your coat.

drift_slip.narration: The crust gives under your first step! You sink to your knees, holding the kid up high. Your party lays the rope across firm rock, and you pull yourself back. Now you can see the hollow, and you skirt its edge. "MEH!" says the kid, outraged, from high above your head.

crust_hold.narration: At the next ridge, the path squeezes under a lip of snow, sagging like a heavy white eyebrow. The kid fits under. Nobody else does, unless somebody holds the snow up. Listen for the creaks, and go in the quiet between them.

interaction.cue: Carry the kid through while the snow lip stops creaking.

onSuccess.narration: The snow lip stays up. The kid trots under, then back again, just to check.

onFailure.narration: The lip sags, then thumps down in a heap, right on top of you. Brrr! Snow down every collar. You dig yourselves out on the far side, and the kid trots out last, quite dry.

onAssisted.narration: You wedge the rope and some stones under the lip. It holds, and everyone gets through.

cairn.narration: Past the drift, a tall pile of stones stands at the foot of the ridge. A flat tin lid peeks out of the snow beneath it, stamped with a little bell. Somebody left it here on purpose. It is frozen hard into the ground. "Hoo-up!" calls the far voice, just over the ridge now.

cairn_dig.prompt: Dig the frozen tin out of the snow with your hands.
cairn_dig.narration: The tin is frozen hard to the ground. The kid helps by digging, badly. "Meh," it says, proud of its work.

onSuccess.narration: You dig and tug, and at last the tin pops out like a cork.

onFailure.narration: You dig until your fingers ache. The tin does not move a hair.

cairn_pry.prompt: Find the right stick and the right spot, and lever the lid loose.
cairn_pry.narration: You slide a stick under the lid and loop the rope around it. Where should you lean?

onSuccess.narration: You lean in just the right spot. The lid pops loose with a crack.

onFailure.narration: Snap! The stick breaks, and the lid stays frozen shut.

cairn_smash.narration: One good bigfoot whack, and the ice falls off in plates. The lid rattles loose. "Meh!" says the kid, and hides behind your boots.

cairn_stuck.narration: Through the frost on the lid, you can read scratched words: "For whoever is lost when the weather turns." Somebody kind left something inside, and it will have to wait for the next lost traveler. The kid licks the lid and gets its tongue stuck for one awful second. Beyond the ridge, something creaks.

cairn_open.narration: Inside are four coins, a candle stub, and a note: "For whoever is lost when the weather turns. Buy something warm. Leave the tin." You take the coins and tuck the tin back. The kid tries to eat the candle. Beyond the ridge, something creaks.

seam_response.narration: The note fades, and so does the trembling. A narrow line of frost lies on the floor under the seam. What do you try?

variants.text: "Not you, not yet," says the herder, kindly. "Let the ice settle after that crack."

seam_hum.narration: You hum, and frost ticks down the seam in time. You stop, and it stops. You start again, and it answers again. The ice stays shut. "That was no accident," says the herder.

seam_touch.narration: You lay your hand on the ice while the yetis hum. A faint tremble reaches your palm, then fades when they stop. You try twice more. Same answer. The seam stays shut. "Funny," says the young singer. "It only does that when we sing."

seam_listen.narration: The herder kneels beside you. You take turns humming and listening. Each time the note sounds, a low ticking answers from the seam. The ice stays shut. "Tick," whispers the young singer. "Tick. Hear it?"

voiceGuide.tone: Warm, funny, curious, with real consequences. Describe actions and sensory details directly. Short dialogue. Never use "the kind of thing that", "the sort of thing that", or "it was X, the type of thing that makes you Y" comparisons. Let a character act instead of explaining how the reader should feel.
voiceGuide.vocabulary: Read aloud to an eight-year-old. Concrete words, short sentences, distinct voices.

npcVoices.Yeti herder: She/her. Female yeti herder and singer. Patient, dry humor, practical cold-weather care; calls her herd with a deep "Hoo-up!". Wants her kid back and her herd fed now the grazing path is water. Witnesses the strange melt and the uphill snow; never explains them, never gives a history or the rifts' cause.
npcVoices.Young yeti singer: Learns and listens; no lore lecture.

shelf_cross.narration: One last pole goes across the snow shelf. "The stream pauses between gulps," says the herder. "Step across when it goes quiet." The stream gulps. Then it goes quiet.

interaction.cue: Step across when the water goes quiet.

onSuccess.narration: You step across in the quiet, plant the pole, and hop back before the next gulp.

onFailure.narration: The stream gulps early and splashes you to the knees. You skip back, dripping. "My turn," says the herder, and plants the pole herself.

onAssisted.narration: The herder counts the gulps aloud. You cross on the count, and the pole goes in.
